# eslint-plugin-secure-coding

Guide for AI coding assistants using this plugin in a project. To change the plugin's own source, read https://github.com/ofri-peretz/eslint/blob/main/AGENTS.md instead.

> ESLint security rules for secure coding — detects LDAP, XPath, XXE, GraphQL and template injection, unsafe deserialization, ReDoS, missing authentication, and PII in logs.

## Enable it

```bash
npm install --save-dev eslint-plugin-secure-coding
```

Requires ESLint ^8.40.0 || ^9.0.0 || ^10.0.0 and Node >=22.13.0.

Flat config files (`eslint.config.*`) are found by ESLint 8.57 and newer; on ESLint 9 and 10 they are the default.

```js
// eslint.config.mjs
import secureCoding from 'eslint-plugin-secure-coding';

export default [secureCoding.configs.recommended];
```

Each preset is one flat config object: put it in the array as an element, do not spread it. Rule ids are prefixed `secure-coding/`. Add it to the config you already have; do not remove other plugins. TypeScript files need a TypeScript parser in the config (`typescript-eslint`).

Use it alongside `eslint-plugin-security`, not instead of it: keep that plugin if the project has it. Measured overlap and the limits of both: https://eslint.interlace.tools/docs/getting-started/with-eslint-plugin-security

## Presets

| Preset               | Rules | Errors | Warnings |
| -------------------- | ----- | ------ | -------- |
| `flagship`           | 2     | 2      | 0        |
| `recommended`        | 18    | 12     | 6        |
| `recommended-strict` | 18    | 18     | 0        |
| `strict`             | 35    | 35     | 0        |
| `owasp-top-10`       | 9     | 7      | 2        |

### `flagship`

2 rules:

- `no-hardcoded-credentials` (error): Detects hardcoded passwords, API keys, tokens, and other sensitive credentials.
- `no-redos-vulnerable-regex` (error): Detects ReDoS-vulnerable regex patterns in literal regex patterns.

### `recommended`

18 rules:

- `no-graphql-injection` (warn): Detects GraphQL injection vulnerabilities and DoS attacks.
- `no-xxe-injection` (error): Detect XML External Entity (XXE) injection vulnerabilities.
- `no-xpath-injection` (error): Detects XPath injection vulnerabilities.
- `no-ldap-injection` (error): Detects LDAP injection vulnerabilities.
- `no-sql-injection` (error): Prevent SQL injection when a query is built from attacker-controlled input and executed through a driver-agnostic handle.
- `no-log-injection` (error): Detects request data concatenated into a log message, which lets an attacker forge log records.
- `no-fail-open-auth` (error): Detects authentication and authorization checks whose catch block fails open.
- `no-homoglyph-identifiers` (error): Detects homoglyph identifiers and invisible characters that hide what the code actually does.
- `no-unsafe-deserialization` (warn): Detects unsafe deserialization of untrusted data.
- `no-redos-vulnerable-regex` (error): Detects ReDoS-vulnerable regex patterns in literal regex patterns.
- `no-unsafe-regex-construction` (error): Detects unsafe regex construction patterns (user input without escaping, dynamic flags).
- `no-hardcoded-credentials` (error): Detects hardcoded passwords, API keys, tokens, and other sensitive credentials.
- `no-template-injection` (error): Disallow dynamic strings as template arguments to server-side template engines (CWE-94).
- `no-improper-sanitization` (error): Detects improper sanitization of user input.
- `no-privilege-escalation` (warn): Detects potential privilege escalation vulnerabilities.
- `no-weak-password-recovery` (warn): Detects weak password recovery mechanisms.
- `no-sensitive-data-exposure` (warn): Detects PII/credentials in logs, responses, or error messages.
- `no-unlimited-resource-allocation` (warn): Detects unlimited resource allocation that could cause DoS.

### `recommended-strict`

Same rules as `recommended`.

### `strict`

Everything in `recommended` plus 17 more (some shared rules run at a different severity here):

- `no-directive-injection` (error): Detects directive injection vulnerabilities in templates.
- `no-format-string-injection` (error): Detects format string injection vulnerabilities.
- `detect-non-literal-regexp` (error): Detects RegExp(variable), which might allow an attacker to DOS your server with a long-running regular expression.
- `detect-object-injection` (error): Detects variable[key] written as an assignment target, or read and then invoked.
- `no-insecure-comparison` (error): Detects insecure comparison operators (==, !=) that can lead to type coercion vulnerabilities.
- `no-improper-type-validation` (error): Detects improper type validation in user input handling.
- `no-missing-authentication` (error): Detects missing authentication checks in route handlers.
- `require-backend-authorization` (error): Require server-side authorization checks.
- `no-pii-in-logs` (error): Prevent PII (email, SSN, credit cards) in console logs.
- `no-unchecked-loop-condition` (error): Detects unchecked loop conditions that could cause DoS.
- `detect-weak-password-validation` (error): Identify weak password requirements.
- `no-electron-security-issues` (error): Detects Electron security vulnerabilities and insecure configurations.
- `no-hardcoded-session-tokens` (error): Detect hardcoded session/JWT tokens.
- `require-secure-defaults` (error): Ensure secure default configurations.
- `no-bidi-characters` (error): Disallows Unicode bidirectional control characters, which let source render differently than it compiles (Trojan Source, CWE-1007).
- `no-invisible-characters` (error): Disallows invisible letters such as the Hangul fillers (U+3164, U+FFA0), which hide identifiers, values and comment text from code review (CWE-1007).
- `no-disabled-template-escaping` (error): Disallows assigning `false` to `escapeMarkup`, which disables template HTML auto-escaping (CWE-79).

### `owasp-top-10`

9 rules:

- `no-privilege-escalation` (warn): Detects potential privilege escalation vulnerabilities.
- `no-hardcoded-credentials` (error): Detects hardcoded passwords, API keys, tokens, and other sensitive credentials.
- `no-sensitive-data-exposure` (warn): Detects PII/credentials in logs, responses, or error messages.
- `no-graphql-injection` (error): Detects GraphQL injection vulnerabilities and DoS attacks.
- `no-xxe-injection` (error): Detect XML External Entity (XXE) injection vulnerabilities.
- `no-xpath-injection` (error): Detects XPath injection vulnerabilities.
- `no-ldap-injection` (error): Detects LDAP injection vulnerabilities.
- `no-weak-password-recovery` (error): Detects weak password recovery mechanisms.
- `no-unsafe-deserialization` (error): Detects unsafe deserialization of untrusted data.

## Other Interlace plugins by dependency

If the project also depends on one of these, add the matching plugin the same way:

- `express`, `fastify`, `koa`, `@hapi/hapi`, `restify`, `hono`, `next`, `@nestjs/core`, `@nestjs/common`, `aws-lambda`, `@types/aws-lambda`, `@middy/core`, `commander`, `yargs`, `@oclif/core`, `@modelcontextprotocol/*`: `eslint-plugin-node-security`
- `express`: `eslint-plugin-express-security`
- `@nestjs/common`, `@nestjs/core`: `eslint-plugin-nestjs-security`
- `react`, `react-dom`, `preact`, `vue`, `svelte`, `@angular/core`, `solid-js`, `lit`, `next`, `nuxt`: `eslint-plugin-browser-security`
- `jsonwebtoken`, `jose`, `express-jwt`, `@nestjs/jwt`, `jwks-rsa`, `jwt-decode`: `eslint-plugin-jwt-security`
- `pg`, `pg-pool`, `pg-promise`, `postgres`, `slonik`: `eslint-plugin-postgresql-security`
- `mysql2`, `mysql`: `eslint-plugin-mysql-security`
- `mongodb`, `mongoose`: `eslint-plugin-mongodb-security`
- `better-sqlite3`, `sqlite3`: `eslint-plugin-sqlite-security`
- `knex`: `eslint-plugin-knex-security`
- `@prisma/client`, `prisma`: `eslint-plugin-prisma-security`
- `drizzle-orm`: `eslint-plugin-drizzle-security`
- `sequelize`: `eslint-plugin-sequelize-security`
- `typeorm`: `eslint-plugin-typeorm-security`
- `@supabase/supabase-js`: `eslint-plugin-supabase-security`
- `@modelcontextprotocol/*`: `eslint-plugin-mcp-sdk-security`
- `openai`, `@openai/agents`: `eslint-plugin-openai-security`
- `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`: `eslint-plugin-anthropic-security`
- `@google/genai`: `eslint-plugin-gemini-security`
- `ai`: `eslint-plugin-vercel-ai-security`
- `aws-lambda`, `@types/aws-lambda`, `@middy/core`: `eslint-plugin-lambda-security`

The full stack-to-plugin playbook (with config rendering and a proof step) is the `security-linting` skill: https://github.com/ofri-peretz/eslint/tree/main/skills/security-linting
